conviction_note: The one clean analogue (the FY25 annual print, 2025-09-09) was -18.78% and all three clean earnings reactions on record are negative (-18.78%, -8.05%, -5.99%); into this print the company has disclosed, on 6k-35k-share sessions that nobody transacted on, that it began deliberately harvesting its publishing business 'during the current quarter', that a $200m shelf went effective on a $44m market cap, and that it is in Nasdaq bid-price deficiency - so I take a negative expectation modestly wider than the baseline's 4.19% but well inside the -18.8% tail, because a profit-up/revenue-down 'AI pivot' framing plus 30k-share liquidity makes a double-digit pop equally mechanically possible.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-12 Gamehaus said it will 'progressively optimize its third-party publishing business in casual titles, and in particular in the social casino category' and manage the existing portfolio 'on a cash flow- and profitability-oriented basis, with user acquisition and operating expenditure allocated according to return on investment rather than scale of installed base' - and that 'This approach took effect during the current quarter', i.e. the July-September quarter now in progress, which is exactly the quarter for which the 2026-09-08 release will issue its forward revenue guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Gamehaus has issued a next-quarter revenue range in every single release (FY25 annual guided Q1 FY26 at $27-30m, Q1 guided Q2 at $24-27m, Q3 guided Q4 at $23-26m) and each of those three prints closed negative, so the guide is the mechanism that moves this stock - and this will be the first guide set after a self-inflicted cut to user acquisition on the company's core business. If the market had processed the 2026-08-12 release, the tape would show it: instead GMHS traded 22,908 shares that day (-5.99%) and 6,192 shares the next (-5.19%) against a genuine typical volume of roughly 10k-70k shares, i.e. the announcement was published into an empty book, and there is no analyst, no consensus estimate and no options market to have translated 'ROI-based UA allocation' into a revenue number. Also unpriced arithmetic: the standing Q4 FY26 guide of $23-26m sits against $30.7m of Q4 FY25 revenue, a 15-25% YoY decline versus the 9.1% decline printed in Q3, and that comparison requires last year's release that nobody has opened.
findings.independence: The Q3 FY2026 release (2026-06-08) independently shows the guide-walk-down and the falling revenue base it is being cut from - Q4 FY26 guided to $23-26m off $26.2m in Q3 - and it is a different document from a different date: http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/gamehaus-holdings-inc-announces-unaudited-financial-results-for-the-third-quarter-of-fiscal-2026-ended-march-31-2026-302793775.html

findings.finding: Three separate structural events sit unabsorbed in front of the print: a $200,000,000 mixed-securities F-3 shelf filed 2026-07-28 and declared effective 2026-08-12 (about 4.5x the ~$44m market cap, with no prospectus supplement drawn as of 2026-09-04), a Nasdaq minimum-bid-price deficiency letter dated 2026-07-10 with a 2027-01-06 compliance deadline and no committed remedy, and a 2026-07-10 extraordinary general meeting that raised Class B voting power from 15 to 50 votes per share - control-proofing the founder immediately before an effective shelf.
findings.why_not_priced: Each disclosure was made into a dead tape: 9,249 shares on 2026-07-13 (the day both the Nasdaq notice and the EGM voting-rights result were published, -2.36%), 13,208 shares on 2026-07-14, 11,904 shares on 2026-07-28 (the shelf filing, -0.82%). A market that had priced a 4.5x-market-cap shelf plus a sub-$1 delisting clock would show a persistent bid-side discount and put-side hedging demand; there are no options on GMHS at all, no analyst coverage, and the 20-day run-up is +0.26% - i.e. nothing in the price says 'dilution and reverse-split risk'. A fiscal-year print with a live 8:00 ET call is the natural venue for either an offering or a share-consolidation intention, and either would land on an audience that has not read the July filings.
findings.independence: Three distinct primary documents from three sources point the same way, so this is not one document read twice: the Nasdaq deficiency PR (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/gamehaus-holdings-inc-receives-nasdaq-notification-regarding-minimum-bid-price-requirement-302823575.html, 2026-07-13) and the 6-K reporting the Class B 15-to-50 vote change (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2000530/000149315226033100/form6-k.htm, 2026-07-14).

findings.finding: The $5m buyback that caused a +105% single-day move when announced on 2025-08-28/30 was 88% unused when it expired: the 2026-08-28 6-K discloses only about 518,063 Class A shares repurchased for roughly $600,000 (an average near $1.16), meaning the company stopped buying entirely as the stock fell from ~$1.16 to a 52-week low near $0.67, and then extended the same authorisation unchanged to 2027-08-28.
findings.why_not_priced: The extension was disclosed only on a 6-K with no accompanying press release I can find, and it moved the stock +0.11% on 66,901 shares - whereas the original announcement of the identical programme moved it +105% on ~46m shares. The market has therefore priced the headline 'buyback' twice and the execution zero times; if it had read the execution it would treat the extension as neutral-to-negative optics rather than support, and the 5-day run-up of +5.77% into the print would not be there. It also sits awkwardly against an effective $200m shelf: a company simultaneously authorising repurchases it does not make and registering securities 4.5x its market cap.
findings.independence: The +105% reaction to the original programme is documented independently by TipRanks on 2025-08-30 (https://www.tipranks.com/news/why-is-gamehaus-stock-gmhs-up-105-today), which is what establishes how much the market credits this instrument versus how little of it was used.

findings.finding: The baseline's 20-day average volume of 405,662 shares is essentially one session: GMHS traded 7,142,358 shares on 2026-08-31 (+16.51%) with no company filing or press release on or around that date, while the surrounding sessions traded 6,192 (2026-08-13), 19,279 (2026-08-11), 22,908 (2026-08-12), 35,144 (2026-08-27) and 66,901 (2026-08-28) shares - so the true book into this print is tens of thousands of shares a day, and the +16.5% spike has already bled off across four consecutive down days to $0.77.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a dispersion finding, not a directional one, and it says the baseline's expected_move_pct of 4.19% is the wrong width. With no options market there is no implied move to correct it, and the 20-day ADV that would normally warn a reader about liquidity has been inflated ~8x by a single unexplained session. If the market were pricing this correctly the name would carry a visible illiquidity discount and a much wider historic reaction distribution than the 4.19% median the baseline reports; instead one 17x-volume day is being read as normal turnover. Practically: a print-day order of ordinary institutional size cannot be filled without moving GMHS by a large multiple of 4.19% in whichever direction it arrives.

searched_and_found_nothing: Third-party mobile-app data for the April-June 2026 quarter - the door the brief said was most worth opening. It is closed for a structural reason worth recording: Gamehaus is a licensor-publisher, and the store accounts bearing its own name carry almost none of its revenue. Google Play 'Gamehaus Network' lists two apps (Whispers: Chapters of Love, 5M+ installs; Bingo Island 2026 Club Bingo, 1M+ installs, 4.4 stars) and Apple 'GAMEHAUS PTE. LTD' lists five (North Tower! Merge TD Defense, Match Tile Scenery, Bingo Island, Vegas Party Casino Slots, Double Win Slots), and a free-tier estimate for Bingo Island on iOS US was ~9k downloads / ~$40k revenue in a month. A company running ~$8.7m of revenue a month cannot be reconstructed from those listings, so publisher-level app data does not map to the P&L. Sources: https://apkcombo.com/developer/Gamehaus%20Network/ and https://apps.apple.com/us/developer/gamehaus-pte-ltd/id1664707862

AppMagic (appmagic.rocks/publisher/gamehaus-network) and Sensor Tower (app.sensortower.com/android/publisher/gamehaus-network) publisher pages render client-side and returned no data through fetch; AppBrain's developer page returned HTTP 403.

Revenue concentration by named title: neither the FY2025 20-F (2025-10-23), the FY2024 20-F, nor the 424B3/F-4 merger prospectus names a single game or discloses what share any title contributes - so the concentration table the screen hoped for does not exist in the filings.

Going-concern or substantial-doubt language: none in the FY2025 20-F, and in any case this 2026-09-08 release is the unaudited annual - the audited 20-F is a separate later filing (FY25's came 2025-10-23), so audit-driven language cannot appear on print day.
Any prospectus supplement, 424B5, ATM or takedown off the effective F-3: nothing filed on EDGAR through 2026-09-04, so the dilution is an overhang and not yet an event.

Any explanation for the 2026-08-31 +16.51% / 7.1m-share session: no filing, no press release, no news item found. This is a strange thing I could not resolve and it is the main reason the upside band on my findings stays open.
Any published EPS or revenue estimate, analyst note or sell-side preview: confirmed absent, consistent with the baseline's n_estimates N/A.

Any 6-K furnishing the Q3 FY2026 results: the Q3 release went out on PR Newswire 2026-06-08 but no corresponding 6-K appears in the EDGAR submissions list between 2026-05-04 and 2026-06-24 - an oddity, but not something I can turn into a tradeable expectation.

Hiring-page, LinkedIn headcount and Form 4 cluster angles: as a foreign private issuer Gamehaus files no Form 4s (only Form 3s, six of them dated 2026-03-18 and one 2026-04-03), so the insider-transaction surface does not exist.
baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with because there is no options market, and the 20-day run-up of +0.26% makes the priced lean flat - so my negative number cuts against a baseline that says nothing, while agreeing with the only clean base rate the baseline does contain (three earnings reactions, all negative, the annual analogue at -18.78%); the one place I contradict the baseline outright is its 4.19% expected move, which I think is far too narrow for a book that trades tens of thousands of shares a day.
